name: OLED display 0.96 inch, 128 x 64, I2C (4 pins)
description: Monochrome OLED module with a 4-pin I2C header (GND, VCC, SCL, SDA), four corner mounting holes, the glass panel's flex cable folded behind the board. Most modules like this use the SSD1306 controller at I2C address 0x3C; the controller on this one is not read yet.

identified.how: from the owner's photos (photos/top.jpg, photos/side.jpg): the printed pin labels GND VCC SCL SDA, four pins on a 2.54 mm header pointing down, the panel and its flex cable. The size (0.96 inch) and the SSD1306 controller are the usual ones for this board, not read from it

mounting: through-hole: one row of 4 male header pins, pointing down from the back; 4 mounting holes

footprint.name: OLED_096_I2C_4P
footprint.why: drill 1.0 mm, pad 1.7 mm: the common 2.54 mm header land. The outline, 27.3 x 27.3 mm (the common size of this module) with the pins 1.4 mm below its top edge (from the top photo): not measured on this one

pitch.source: a standard 2.54 mm header (the photo, scaled by the board's holes, agrees); not measured

board.source: the common size of this module in sellers' listings (27.3 x 27.3, 27.3 x 27.8; other makers 26 or 28 square); the owner: a standard 0.96 inch module, 2026-11-19; not measured on this one

holes.value: 4, 2.0 mm diameter, near the corners; spacing not known
holes.source: diameter from DFRobot's SSD1306 module page (a similar module); no listing gives the spacing: measure before the box

pin_numbering: 1-4 from left to right, seen from the front with the pins at the top
pins: ground. Check the label: on some modules VCC comes first, and swapping them can kill the display
supply, 3.3 V to 5 V on most modules (a regulator on the back); not checked on this one
I2C clock (on the ESP32 by convention G22)
I2C data (on the ESP32 by convention G21)
